chunks: Tamim ibn Abd Allah ibn Tamim al-Qurashi (RA) said: My father narrated to us, from Ahmad ibn Ali al-Ansari, from Abu al-Salt Abd al-Salam ibn Salih al-Hirawi, who said: Al-Ma'mun asked Ali ibn Musa al-Rida (AS) one day

He said to him: O son of the Messenger of Allah, what is the meaning of the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: (And if your Lord had willed, all those who are in the earth would have believed, all of them; will you then force men till they become believers? And it is not for a soul to believe except by Allah's permission)

Al-Rida (AS) replied: My father Musa ibn Ja'far narrated to me, from his father Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father Muhammad ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn al-Husayn, from his father al-Husayn ibn Ali, from his father Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS)

That the Muslims said to the Messenger of Allah (SAWW): O Messenger of Allah, if you compelled the people over whom you had power to embrace Islam, our numbers would increase and we would be strong against our enemy.
The Messenger of Allah (SAWW) replied: I would not face Allah, the Mighty and High, with an innovation for which no instruction had been revealed to me, and I am not among those who force (people).

So Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, revealed: O Muhammad, (And if your Lord had willed, all those who are in the earth would have believed, all of them) through compulsion and constraint in this world, as they will believe upon direct observation and seeing the hardship in the Hereafter.

And if you compelled them to do so, they would not deserve any reward or praise from Me, but I want them to believe choosing freely, not being compelled, so that they may earn My Proximity and Honor, and eternal life in Paradise.

(Will you then force men till they become believers?) And as for His Word, the Mighty and High: (And it is not for a soul to believe except by Allah's permission), this is not on the basis of forbidding belief upon it.

But rather on the meaning that it does not believe except by Allah's permission, and His permission is His command for it to believe, when it is not burdened with obligation, and His compelling it to belief occurs when the obligation and burden are removed from it.
Al-Ma'mun said: You have relieved me, O Abu al-Hasan. May Allah relieve you!

key_terms.التَّكْلِيفُ: Obligation or burden of religious duty
key_terms.الرِّضَا: Al-Rida, title of Imam Ali ibn Musa

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'And it is not for a soul to believe except by Allah's permission' in Shia theology?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (AS) elucidates that divine compulsion (al-ijbāl) refers to the overwhelming certainty of faith at the moment of death or resurrection, whereas the current life is a realm of free choice (ikhtiyār) necessary for earning reward. He clarifies that 'except by Allah's permission' denotes God's command enabling belief once the burden of obligation (taklīf) is lifted, rather than a restriction on the soul's inherent capacity. This explanation, delivered to Caliph al-Ma'mun, reinforces the Shia doctrine of free will within divine decree, distinguishing between predestination of the outcome and the voluntary nature of the act.
